title: Preflight ASK-1: adversarial reviewer not set in config.toml — answer a provider (installed: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `agy`, `opencode:<model>`), as `<provider>`, `<provider>:<model>` or `<provider>:<model>:<effort>`, to give every run a cross-vendor second opinion from it; `none` disables cross-vendor review; both are saved to config.toml for every repo. `proceed` skips the second opinion for this run only and leaves config.toml unset
body:
**Chose:** cursor
**Because:** the owner's answer to a preflight ask, before any slice started.
**Review:** no

title: Codex input excludes its cached part; OpenCode reasoning counts inside output
body:
**Chose:** the Codex normalizer stores `input_tokens - cached_input_tokens` as `input_tokens` (cached goes to `cache_read_input_tokens`), and the OpenCode normalizer stores `output + reasoning` as `output_tokens` with `reasoning` as thinking tokens.
**Over:** copying `usage.input_tokens` and `tokens.output` verbatim.
**Because:** OpenAI-style input counts already include the cached part, and OpenCode reports reasoning apart from output; Claude's `Usage` excludes cache from input and includes thinking in output, so the verbatim copy would weigh Codex cache reads at full price in `budget_weighted_tokens` and drop OpenCode reasoning from it.
**Undo:** take out the `saturating_sub` in the `turn.completed` arm and the `add(.., reasoning)` in the `step_finish` arm of `src/stream.rs`.

title: Does a --worker flag that switches a role's provider keep config.toml's model and effort?
body:
**Chose:** no — a role takes `[workers.<role>]` model/effort only when its resolved provider equals that role's config provider (`[workers.<role>] provider`, else `[workers] provider`, else `FACTORY_WORKER_PROVIDER`), and `[workers]` model/effort only when it equals `[workers] provider` (else the env). Otherwise the provider's defaults apply.
**Over:** taking `[workers.<role>]` model/effort whenever set, as the FR's literal precedence list reads.
**Because:** a role model is a provider-specific slug; `--worker build=codex` over `[workers.build] provider = "claude", model = "sonnet"` must not hand `sonnet` to codex — the same rule FR-1 states for `[workers]`.
**Undo:** drop the `own` guard in `config::resolve_role`.

title: Touch src/worker.rs for the new WorkerRef.provider field?
body:
**Chose:** one line, `provider: None`, in the `WorkerRef` literal at `src/worker.rs` (and in `tests/run.rs`'s `worker_ref`).
**Over:** leaving `src/worker.rs` untouched as the slice asks, which cannot compile once `WorkerRef` gains a field.
**Because:** the slice orders `WorkerRef.provider`; a struct literal must name every field. Spawning is unchanged; slice 03 sets the real provider.
**Undo:** slice 03 replaces `None` with the spawned worker's provider.

title: Do --worker flags on a run that parks on the worker ask survive the answer?
body:
**Chose:** no — answering the worker ask resolves `worker_config` from the saved `config.toml` (`<provider>` answer) or the first detected CLI (`proceed`); `--worker` specs given to that `factory run` are not re-applied.
**Over:** persisting the raw specs on the run so the answer layers them back on.
**Because:** the ask fires only when a role still has no provider after the flags, so this is the partial-flag case (`--worker build=codex` with nothing else set); RunState has no place for raw specs and the slice names none. Passing an all-role `--worker` avoids the ask entirely.
**Undo:** save `args.workers` beside `preflight.json` and pass them to `config::resolve_workers` in `worker_answer`.

title: When does factory setup workers treat a provider change as a switch?
body:
**Chose:** a table that names no provider (nor inherits one from `[workers]`) counts as Claude, so `--provider claude` on a legacy `[workers] model = "sonnet"` keeps the model, while `--provider codex` drops it unless `--model`/`--effort` is given.
**Over:** treating a provider-less table as unknown and clearing its model on any `--provider`.
**Because:** before workers had a provider every `[workers]` slug was Claude's (`config::inherit_worker_defaults` reads it that way too).
**Undo:** `table_now` in `src/cli/setup.rs`: drop the `unwrap_or(Provider::Claude)`.

title: provider::tests::discover_models_parses_live_outputs_and_kills_hung_probe flakes under the full suite
body: It writes a script then execs it while other test threads fork (ETXTBSY-style race), and once returned `[]` for agy; `cargo test -q --lib discover_models` alone passes every time — rerun the loop before chasing it.

title: Does the git shim catch an alias that expands to a push?
body:
**Chose:** no — the `run_dir/bin/git` shim judges only the literal subcommand after git's global options (`--attr-source` counted with the value-taking ones; any other unknown `-x` option is read as a flag), so `git -c alias.p=push p` or a repo alias reaches real git.
**Over:** resolving every unknown subcommand through `git config --get alias.<name>` before exec.
**Because:** that costs a second git process on every worker git call; `push_off_env` still rewrites every git@/ssh/https/http/git remote, so only an alias aimed at a remote with an explicit non-network `pushurl` gets through, the same class of gap as the absolute-path `/usr/bin/git` bypass the PRD accepts.
**Undo:** in `GIT_SHIM` (`src/worker.rs`), add an alias lookup for a subcommand that is not a builtin.

title: Touch src/provider.rs to probe versions and key them by Provider?
body:
**Chose:** derive `PartialOrd, Ord` on `Provider` so `provider_versions` is the `BTreeMap<Provider, String>` the slice names, make `run_bounded` `pub(crate)` so `probe_provider_versions` reuses its process-group 5 s timeout, and have `run_bounded` drop `CLAUDECODE` for every probe (model listings included).
**Over:** a string-keyed map and a second copy of the bounded runner in `src/cli/run.rs`.
**Because:** the slice asks to reuse the process-group timeout logic, which lives private in `src/provider.rs`; dropping `CLAUDECODE` from a `models`/`--list-models` call of a non-Claude CLI changes nothing for it.
**Undo:** revert the derive and the `pub(crate)`/`env_remove` lines in `src/provider.rs` and inline a bounded runner in `src/cli/run.rs`.

title: Which token of a --version line does factory report print?
body:
**Chose:** the first whitespace-separated token that starts with a digit, else the first token (`2.1.296 (Claude Code)` → `2.1.296`, `codex-cli 0.172.0` → `0.172.0`); `runs.knobs` stores the first non-empty line of `<bin> --version` verbatim.
**Over:** the literal first token the slice names.
**Because:** real Codex prints `codex-cli <ver>`, so the first token would render `codex codex-cli` instead of the slice's own example `codex 0.172.0`; legacy rows keep the old first-token `claude <ver>` rendering unchanged.
**Undo:** `version_number` in `src/cli/report.rs`: return `v.split_whitespace().next()`.

title: What runs.knobs holds before the worker ask is answered, and where each role's sources come from
body:
**Chose:** a run parked on the worker ask records `"workers": {}` and `"provider_versions": {}` (nothing probed); answering it rewrites `workers`, `provider_versions` and `claude_version` (a `proceed` answer labels every part `default`), printing any probe warning on the answer's stdout. Each role's `provider_source`/`source`/`effort_source` is the first layer (flag, role table, `[workers]`) that holds the value the role resolved to, else `default`. `review` is `null` when nobody chose a reviewer and is not rewritten when the review ask is answered.
**Over:** leaving the parked run's knobs empty for good, or re-deriving sources from the env as `resolve_workers` does.
**Because:** the slice asks for the refresh on the worker answer only; matching values keeps a `FACTORY_WORKER_PROVIDER` the loaded sources cannot see from being labelled `user`.
**Undo:** `config::role_sources` and `cli::run::set_worker_knobs` (call sites in `src/cli/answer.rs`).

title: Update the per-worker line pinned in tests/metrics.rs?
body:
**Chose:** yes — `ctx_calls_are_labelled_and_the_report_reads_the_reversal_rule` now expects `worker <id> build claude slice 01 (...)` and ` build claude slice 02 `.
**Over:** leaving the provider off the per-worker line.
**Because:** the PRD orders the provider on every `--per-worker` line; the assertion is as strict as before, now naming the provider too.
**Undo:** drop `{provider}` from `PerWorker::text` and revert the two strings in `tests/metrics.rs`.
